transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Torres (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Maya Chen (Sundial Head of Platform), Ethan Rivera (Sundial ML Eng), Priya Das (Sundial Security), Omar Ruiz (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Sundial Works' path from prototype to production. They want a fast path (PLG/self-serve) to validate features with hosted API and a decision tree for moving to Dedicated or Private deployment depending on latency and data residency/security needs. Discussed free credits, time-to-first-token (TTFT), benchmarking plan, and security gating (SSO, KMS, audit logs).

Topics:
- Self-serve quickstart and free credits
- Time-to-first-token expectations and sample SDK snippets
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit for Sundial
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, EU residency
- Next steps and benchmark plan

Action items (brief): see metadata action_items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Maya, you on?
[00:05] Maya: Yep, here. Thanks Samir. We appreciate you squeezing us in.
[00:08] Samir: Of course. Quick intros, we'll keep it tight -- Nina's our SE, Liam's on architecture. Could you give a quick rundown of where Sundial is with the ML feature and what success looks like?
[00:20] Maya: Sure. We're building a contextual help assistant inside the Sundial dashboard — mostly retrieval-augmented answers on customer config and logs. We have a prototype using off-the-shelf hosted endpoints but latency's a bit high for some flows. Goal is to ship a beta in 6–8 weeks and keep cost under control.
[00:38] Omar: And important for us — lots of EU customers so data residency matters, plus we need strict audit logs for support interactions.
[00:45] Nina: Got it. So short path is hosted Redwood API for fastest time to first token (TTFT), we can get you started with self-serve and credits — then Dedicated or Private if you need capacity isolation or on-prem/VPC.
[00:55] Ethan: How quick is TTFT? From sign-up to making the first request?
[00:59] Samir: In practice, with the quickstart we've seen teams do first call in under 15 minutes — that's signup, grab API key, run curl or SDK snippet, stream a response. If you want to integrate into your CI or app, plan on a few hours.
[01:12] Ethan: Nice. The prototype was using another provider — we saw about 400–600ms median for short prompts; is Redwood competitive there?
[01:19] Nina: It depends on the model and tokenization. For comparable open models on hosted Redwood, median latencies for single-turn prompts often sit in 200–350ms region on optimal configs. But that varies if you need longer context or embeddings. Also batching decisions impact per-token latency.
[01:36] Priya: Can I ask about data retention and encryption? We need support data not retained beyond 30 days and customer data at rest encrypted with a key we control.
[01:44] Liam: For hosted, we support configurable retention windows and Redwood has KMS integrations for enterprise — you can bring your own keys for certain tiers. Private deployment gives you full control. We'll share the SOC2 and the KMS integration docs after this call.
[02:05] Maya: You mentioned Dedicated — what's the difference vs hosted in terms of cost and throughput?
[02:10] Samir: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput and better tail latency for steady traffic. Cost is higher than hosted on a pure variable usage basis, but unit cost can be lower at scale if you commit. Hosted is great for quickstart and spiky PLG traffic.
[02:24] Omar: For EU residency, would Hosted in a Europe region be sufficient or is Private required?
[02:29] Nina: Hosted EU region often satisfies data residency if you keep data and compute in-region and use region-specific retention policies. For stringent legal contracts or on-prem requirements, Private is the route.
[02:40] Ethan: We also want to run a perf benchmark against a set of 5,000 typical prompts — can Redwood run that and show throughput/latency/cost per 1k tokens?
[02:49] Nina: Absolutely. Typical approach: you share the sample prompts and payload sizes, we schedule a 60-minute run with an SE to capture medians, p95/p99, and token-level cost. We'll also show suggestions — batching settings and quantization profiles to reduce unit cost.
[03:06] Maya: How do SDKs look? Our stack is node/python.
[03:09] Samir: SDKs for both; quickstart includes copy-paste snippets. Example curl and node snippet will be in the guide I send. Streamed responses supported in SDKs.
[03:18] Omar: We're also evaluating Anthropic and MajorCloudAI — any immediate differentiation?
[03:22] Samir: Two quick points: Redwood is inference-platform-first — we give you the runtime knobs (batching, caching, quantization recommendations) and observability into per-route token cost and latency. We also unify hosted/dedicated/private under same API and rollout controls, so migrating from hosted to private is less friction.
[03:42] Priya: For audit logs and traceability, is there per-request tracing and SAML SSO for access?
[03:48] Liam: Yes on request tracing and long retention is an add-on. We support SSO/SAML and role-based access for the console and API. We'll include example audit log outputs in the security pack.
[04:01] Ethan: Any gotchas on prefix caching or KV cache for dialogs? We worry about token inflation when conversational state gets big.
[04:09] Nina: We have prefix caching primitives — you can cache embeddings or KV for static context and the runtime can avoid re-sending prefix tokens. For long-running conversations, strategies include chunking or storing summaries; we'll suggest approaches after we see your flows.
[04:24] Maya: About the credits — what's included in the free credits for trial? Is it model-agnostic?
[04:29] Samir: Credits are dollar-denominated; you can use them across the hosted catalog for generation and embeddings. There are some limits for enterprise-only models, but for evaluation you should be able to run the perf test. We'll include how to redeem in the guide.
[04:41] Omar: Ok, what is the expected uplift we might see moving to Dedicated? If our latency is noisy on hosted, will Dedicated guarantee p99?
[04:48] Samir: Dedicated gives much stronger tail behavior because you control the pool, autoscaling policy, and you avoid multi-tenant noisy neighbors. We give SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated customers depending on commitment level. We can propose numbers after the benchmark.
[05:03] Priya: Are there limits on bringing your own model/artifacts if we want to run a fine-tuned checkpoint?
[05:07] Nina: You can bring models into Private or Dedicated in many cases; we have onboarding guardrails around compatibility and quantization. For hosted, bringing arbitrary large checkpoints is harder — but you can use hosted catalog plus private model hosting in Dedicated/Private.
[05:22] Ethan: How do we start? If we sign up today, what's the TTFT timeline and what's required from us to get the benchmark scheduled?
[05:29] Samir: If you sign up, we send credits and quickstart link. For the benchmark: share sample prompts, payload sizes, and a preferred window; Nina will schedule an SE-driven run. Typical TTFT to first call: under 15 minutes. Full perf run scheduling usually happens within a week.
[05:44] Maya: We're targeting a beta mid-May, which is about 6 weeks out. We'll want to lock a path by mid-April. Does that timeline make sense?
[05:51] Liam: Yes—if we get the benchmark and initial security Qs this week, we can help you pick hosted vs Dedicated within two weeks.
[05:58] Omar: Any documentation we should review right away?
[06:01] Samir: I'll send a short quickstart doc, the credits redemption guide, and an architecture note on differences between modes. Nina will attach the security pack.
[06:10] Priya: Can we get a sample contract excerpt for data processing terms?
[06:14] Samir: Yes, procurement/legal can provide a DPA example; I'll include a pointer but we'll loop in legal after the technical validation.
[06:22] Ethan: Minor thing — does Redwood expose token-level breakdown per route in the console? We want to see which screens cost us the most.
[06:29] Nina: Yes, per-route and per-token cost breakdowns, plus traces for latency. You can tag requests by route.
[06:34] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[06:36] Samir: I think that's it from our side. Quick recap and we'll call out owners.
[06:40] Nina: Recap: Samir sends quickstart + credits; Nina sends security pack and schedules benchmark after Sundial uploads prompts. Sundial owners: Ethan uploads prompts, Priya sends residency/compliance asks.
[06:52] Omar: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[06:55] Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up by email with links and a proposed benchmark window.
[07:00] Recording ends.

Notes on transcript quality: There are a few mis-transcribed names and occasional overlaps; filler words preserved.
